key_insight: MATTRL enables multi-agent LLM teams to adapt at test time by injecting structured textual experience into their deliberation loop, achieving robust reasoning improvements without costly, unstable multi-agent RL training.
problem_solved: Addresses the resource intensity, instability (co-adaptation / non-stationarity), and sparse/high-variance reward issues of conventional multi-agent RL for LLM-driven collaborators by shifting adaptation to a lightweight test-time procedure.
method: Run multiple LLM agents in a deliberation loop and log structured textual experiences (dialogue turns, proposed actions, outcomes, and rewards).

Inject these textual experiences back into the deliberation at test time to shape behavior (guided sampling, credit assignment, or reward shaping) so agents adapt on-the-fly without full MARL retraining.
Use cross-checking and aggregated signals from diverse agents to stabilize learning and reduce variance in sparse-reward reasoning tasks.
impact: MATTRL lets practitioners obtain stronger, more robust multi-agent reasoning with far less compute and training complexity, enabling practical deployment of collaborative LLM systems that adapt in real-world inference settings.
